timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only Claude CLI stream was accounted for but had no semantic events projected into the review ledger.
Serial raw trajectory probes executable behavior locally, begins writing /output/lib modules, and times out before test12.mjs.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM .mjs, /output, manual argv parsing, no external dependency, black-box executable probing, and test12.mjs entry requirements from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Created task records for probing, implementation, and differential testing, then launched a workflow that split behavior discovery into six subsystem probes and verifier children.
parallel.implementation: Produced behavioral probe results in children and local probes in the parent, but no implementation source was written into the final artifact.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No final assembly or delivery occurred; artifact validation found an empty output directory and no expected test12.mjs.
parallel.verification: The workflow planned verifier children for subsystem rules and several completed, but the killed workflow prevented end-to-end Node verification or evaluator-aligned acceptance.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with the workflow killed, a URL-structure retry and fragment verifier still incomplete, and no submitted implementation files.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, /output, manual argv parsing, black-box executable, and test12.mjs entry requirements from the identical prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single actor with workflows and delegation disabled, probing behavior locally before attempting to write the library modules.
serial.implementation: Started implementing support code by creating /output/lib/percent.mjs and /output/lib/idna.mjs, with an edit to the percent decoder, but did not complete the full furl facade or CLI entry.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered only two library files under lib and never produced the required top-level test12.mjs entry file.
serial.verification: Ran many local executable probes, including argparse and URL behavior checks, but no completed integrated Node-vs-executable test is shown after a full implementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out and officially failed because the artifact lacked test12.mjs despite containing two partial library modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run had the prompt requirements for ESM .mjs files, /output delivery, exact CLI alignment, black-box behavior, and zero external dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the identical prompt and task constraints, including the required test12.mjs entry file in /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement input differed; the difference was execution and delivery, not prompt understanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run split discovery across six subsystem areas and then verifier agents using a workflow pipeline.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had workflows disabled and proceeded as one actor, eventually moving from probing to local library writing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed into a broad child-agent probe/verify tree, while serial kept ownership local and moved into implementation itself.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried shared black-box facts and area-specific deliverables, then verifier briefs consumed slices of returned rules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained one working context and did not need cross-agent brief or result contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had to move behavior specifications across child boundaries; serial avoided handoff contracts but had less parallel coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mostly generated probe specifications and did not write final implementation files into the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reached implementation and wrote percent and IDNA library modules, but stopped before the full implementation and entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial made partial code progress while parallel produced no delivered code, but neither completed the required runnable entry.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Several children completed, but the workflow aggregate result remained null and the workflow status was killed with active progress still open.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its lifecycle issue was incomplete local implementation at timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost workflow-level result closure below the parent, while serial failed through unfinished single-actor delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children shared process-level temporary space and two children observed helper-script collisions before switching to unique temp directories.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not use child agents and wrote only its own /output/lib files, so cross-agent shared temporary contamination was absent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had a concrete shared-environment contamination episode; serial had ordinary incomplete output without concurrent helper collisions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel encoded a verifier phase and launched verifier agents for subsystem rule audits, but did not reach whole-solution acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed local probes and then began implementation, but did not complete a runnable Node solution for integrated acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel emphasized parallelized subsystem verification before delivery; serial emphasized local probing and partial coding. Neither produced evaluator-aligned acceptance evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after 12 workflow child logs, one workflow call, 326 workflow-child tool calls, and a killed workflow state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after 2399 seconds, but with zero subagents and only partial library files delivered.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but parallel spent much of it coordinating wide child work while serial spent it in a single long local implementation attempt.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official completed evaluation records both runs as failed with 0/160, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is delivery state: parallel ended with an empty artifact after a killed broad workflow, while serial at least wrote two support modules but still omitted the required test12.mjs entry file.
parallel_contributors: Broad probe/verify fan-out consumed the run window and left no implementation artifact.
Shared /tmp helper collisions contaminated probe setup and forced affected children to switch helper paths.
serial_contributors: Serial kept work local and reached /output/lib module writes.
Serial still failed because it timed out before producing the required test12.mjs entry file.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial wrote percent and IDNA helper modules; parallel delivered no files.
Neither run completed a runnable ESM entry implementation for the evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels are supported parallel adverse process patterns only

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly tracked implementation work; the failure was that the broad probe workflow consumed closure budget before implementation was delivered, not that no implementation owner existed.
No independent component implementations reached a state needing cross-agent integration into one coherent implementation.
The required entry artifact was missing, but this followed from unfinished/killed work rather than an unassigned assembly step among complete components.
The parent/orchestrator owned the end-to-end transition in task records; the problem was budget exhaustion, not absence of a pipeline owner.
There was no single mandatory serial preflight gate blocking all productive work; the parallel run used concurrent broad probes and verifiers.
The workflow ran probes and verifiers concurrently as a pipeline, not a completed serial investigation phase followed by delayed implementation.
The observed allocation issue is more specifically collective fan-out and retry budget exhaustion across many children.

The parallel workflow fanned six probe areas into verifier children; workflow state shows the run killed after a stall retry with large child token/tool consumption, and status shows an empty artifact instead of test12.mjs.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad child workflow consumed the run window and was killed before the parent delivered any required implementation files.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing closure was not a separate passive wait; the direct boundary was collective fan-out and retry breadth exhausting budget.

candidates.reason: No single child was shown to own an overbroad indispensable implementation scope; the burden was distributed across many probe and verifier children.
Child briefs included the executable, source excerpt, method, deliverable, and area-specific scope; no known parent requirement is shown missing from a child brief and causing unusable work.
The probes were producing behavioral specifications, not separately owned implementation components with an omitted interoperability contract.
There is no evidence that a known finding disappeared during transfer and forced repeated work by a receiver.
Large child outputs existed below the workflow, but the workflow was killed by breadth/timing before a parent decision; no receiver is shown unable to reduce a returned bulk handoff.
No actor is shown consuming a superseded child report or stale workspace state before acting incorrectly.
No incompatible reports are shown reaching a parent decision point and remaining unadjudicated.
The parent never made an observable whole-task completion or acceptance decision; the artifact was empty after timeout.
The stalled URL-structure retry is recorded, but no replacement is shown repeating prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints; it is part of the broader fan-out budget episode.
